name: Final Reel
best_for: childhood nostalgia, familiar faces, child stars and celebrities, tragic endings, 'where are they now', memorial lists
look: A film-archive memorial. Charcoal and ivory with a muted gold for what they were known for and one crimson for the ending. Names in Playfair, labels in condensed caps, dates on a typewriter. Portraits in ivory film frames with sprocket holes over the same photo blurred and dark; borrowed clips play inside the frame, never full screen. Fast cold open (1.5-2 s cuts, a wall of faces), then a slow documentary body: one person = castcard -> their roles (framed clips, photos) -> the turn -> ageclock -> memoriam.

devices.use: Who this is - one per person: framed portrait, rank, name wiping in, the role they are remembered for, years, age chip.
The age they died at, counting up, with the date and one line. Use on 'He was twenty-three.'
Closing card for the people whose story lands hardest: black-and-white portrait in an arch, years, one line.
A wall of faces filling in: the cold open ('thirty-five young performers'), the roll call at the end.
A life on one line: born -> roles -> the end, each marker on its word. For lives with several turning points.
Borrowed show / film clips play INSIDE the film frame (clip with inset=[x,y,w,h]), 2-4 s, silent, never full screen.
Name + role over a full-screen photo or B-roll when the face is not introduced by a castcard.
Where it happened (the Viper Room, London, New Orleans): a dark map with one pin.
A line they said or a line from their role, set as a quote.
Depth pop on the best portrait of a person.

rules: Cold open: first 45-60 s fast - 1.5-2 s cuts, framed clips and photos, a rollcall on the count of names. Then slow: 5-8 s shots, soft dissolves.
One person = castcard on their name -> the roles (framed clips 2-4 s, photos with slow pushes) -> the turn (photos, B-roll) -> ageclock on the age -> memoriam for the heaviest endings.
About 30 % moving footage (framed borrowed clips + B-roll), 70 % pictures and graphics.
Borrowed show / film clips: short (2-4 s), silent, inside the reelframe (or flipped / cropped), always under narration, never full screen.
Every age at death is an ageclock or the castcard's age chip; every named place of death that matters gets a map.
No interviews / talking heads, no thumbnails or memes, no logos or other channels' captions (QC people mode enforces it).
Facts only as the script states them; never show a living person as dead.
